Test file: src/claim-office.spec.ts
Implementation file: src/claim-office.ts
Passing tests: 14
Recent Green phase: added an `Item` type with an optional `cursed` flag, and `itemSurchargesOf` which charges 50% of a cursed item's own base premium. `quote` now sums the policy-wide first-insurance surcharge and the item-specific surcharges against the unmodified base rather than compounding them.

Refactor the implementation while keeping all tests green. Run tests with `pnpm test`. Also keep `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.

Key domain rule now visible in the code — worth shaping the design around: ALL percentage modifiers are computed against the unmodified base and SUMMED, never compounded. Item-specific modifiers (cursed, and soon high-enchantment) use the affected ITEM's base premium; policy-wide modifiers (first insurance, and soon loyalty and follow-up discounts) use the POLICY base premium. Only the final premium is rounded (up), then a flat 5 G fee is added.

Both `increasedBy` and `percentOf` now exist and are near-duplicates; consider whether expressing everything as summed `percentOf` deltas is cleaner than the `increasedBy` form, given the summing rule above.

Percentages must stay in integer percent points — `base * 1.1` yields 110.00000000000001 and breaks the ceil.

Known and deliberate, do NOT fix: the block discount applies to any type at count 3, including main items; unknown item types yield NaN. Both await their own Red phases.

Run autonomously, return when done.

content.text:
Refactor phase complete. All 14 tests green, `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.

**Implementation file**: `/home/experimenter/experiments/runs/2026-09-04_14-03-39_claim-office-example-mapping_v6.1.4-continuation-guard-cc_opus-5-no-thinking/src/claim-office.ts`

## Naming evaluation (done first)

`withFirstInsuranceSurcharge` was the one name that no longer fit. The `with…` form promises "the base *with* the surcharge folded in" — a whole-value, compounding shape. But the domain rule is that modifiers are *summed deltas against an unmodified base*. So it returned `base + delta` while its sibling `itemSurchargesOf` returned a bare `delta`, and `quote` was adding two structurally different kinds of number. The name was actively pointing away from the rule.

Renamed to `policyModifiersOf` (returns the delta), with `itemSurchargesOf` → `itemModifiersOf` to match. The pair now reads as one concept at two scopes, and `quote` reads as the rule itself:

```typescript
const modifiers =
  policyModifiersOf(policyBase) +
  items.reduce((total, item) => total + itemModifiersOf(item), 0);

return Math.ceil(policyBase + modifiers) + PROCESSING_FEE;
```

`policyBase` now appears exactly once as the thing modifiers are measured against — the "never compounded" rule is visible in the shape rather than only in a comment.

## Rule 3 — duplication

Deleted `increasedBy` entirely. It was a near-duplicate of `percentOf` (`increasedBy(a,p) === a + percentOf(a,p)`), and under the summing rule it was the wrong shape, not merely redundant — keeping it would invite a future modifier to be written in compounding form. One percentage primitive remains. Its comment now carries both invariants (summed-against-unmodified-base, and integer percent points).

`itemModifiersOf` also changed arity from `Item[]` to a single `Item`, moving the fold up into `quote`. Both scopes' modifier logic now sits at the same level of `quote`, and adding high-enchantment means one more term in a single-item function.

## APP mass

Scoped to the functions touched (`increasedBy`, `percentOf`, `withFirstInsuranceSurcharge`, `itemSurchargesOf`, `quote`); the `countByType`/`baseOfGroup`/`policyBaseOf` group is unchanged.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Constants | 5 | 3 |
| Bindings | 12 | 11 |
| Invocations | 6 (12) | 6 (12) |
| Conditionals | 1 (4) | 1 (4) |
| Loops | 1 (5) | 1 (5) |
| Assignments | 0 | 0 |
| **Total** | **50** | **45** |

Δ −5, from deleting `increasedBy` (mass 5) with no compensating growth — the fold moved rather than duplicated. Rule 2 was the driver here and the mass reduction followed; had they conflicted I'd have kept the clearer form.

## Left alone deliberately

Per your instruction: the block discount applying to main items at count 3, and `NaN` for unknown item types. Both are reachable through `BASE_PREMIUMS[type]` returning `undefined` and await their own Red phases — I did not add guards, since doing so would write untested behaviour and pre-empt those tests.

One observation for when the loyalty and follow-up discounts arrive: `policyModifiersOf` currently takes only `policyBase`, but those two need customer years and step index. That signature will have to widen — I left it narrow rather than speculatively threading a context object through, since nothing tests it yet.
